# Planner — Progress Memory

> **This file is the agent's persistent memory.** The `Planner` agent
> (`.github/agents/planner.agent.md`) MUST read this at session start and update it at session
> end. Keep it accurate and current. Commit it together with the work it describes.

## Mission

Turn each changelog feature (from the Changelog Researcher's backlog) into a concrete,
step-by-step implementation plan for the `llm` VS Code extension. The planner does NOT write
code — only the Coder writes code.

## Active plan — 1.101-4 · MCP support for sampling (Experimental) (VS Code 1.101)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — MCP servers can make **sampling requests** back to the model (the server asks the LLM to generate text); confirmation on first use; configurable model access per server; request log. Relevance: keep (capability/context) — MCP capability. Gap: no sampling support. Extend: handle `sampling/createMessage` JSON-RPC requests from the server; forward to the local model; return the result.
- **Approach:** MCP sampling is the reverse direction of every existing MCP feature: the SERVER sends a JSON-RPC *request* (`sampling/createMessage`, with a numeric `id`) and expects a *response* written back on the same channel. Today `McpJsonRpc.handleLine` treats any message whose id is not pending as a notification and drops it — so the first change is a new `onRequest` hook (method + params + a `respond({ result } | { error })` callback) that lets the client answer server-initiated requests. `McpClient` (stdio) wires `onRequest` to a `sampling/createMessage` handler that delegates to a host-provided callback (`setSamplingHandler`); `McpHttpClient` (Streamable HTTP) detects server requests inside the SSE/JSON response body (a message with a numeric `id` different from the client's own pending id AND a string `method`) and answers by POSTing the response back (echoing `Mcp-Session-Id`). `McpManager` owns the policy layer: a per-server allow/deny map (`setSamplingAllowed(name, allowed)` — the "configurable model access per server" kept minimal as a boolean, NOT a model picker), an in-memory request log (`samplingLog: McpSamplingLogEntry[]`, capped at 100, `getSamplingLog()`), and `setSamplingHandler(cb)` which registers ONE handler on every running client and on clients started later via `ensureStarted`. The per-client handler: denied server → JSON-RPC error `sampling denied for server '<name>'`; otherwise → invoke the host callback (which does the confirmation + model round-trip) and return its result, or a JSON-RPC error on failure. Every request (allowed or denied) is appended to the log. Host side (`ChatViewProvider`): the callback checks `llm.mcp.sampling.confirm` (default `true`) — when on and this server has not been confirmed this session (in-memory `Set<string>`), it posts a `sampling_request` card to the webview (server name, requested model, max tokens, message count) and awaits the user's `sampling_approval` reply; deny → JSON-RPC error. On approval it builds a plain `ChatCompletionRequest` from the MCP params via the pure `mcpSamplingParamsToMessages` helper (system→system, user→user, assistant→assistant; `systemPrompt` prepended as a leading system message; `maxTokens` → `max_completion_tokens`; `model` → `model` when non-empty, else the active model), runs `this.client.chatStream(body)` (no tools, no streaming UI — accumulate `content` deltas), and returns `{ role: "assistant", content: { type: "text", text } }`. Each request is also written to the extension's output channel (the "request log"). New settings: `llm.mcp.sampling.confirm` (boolean, default `true`) and `llm.mcp.sampling.allowed` (object map server→boolean, default `{}` = allow all). No new deps, no bundler, one webview.
- **Files to touch:** `src/mcp.ts`, `src/mcpManager.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `src/chat/webview.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/presets.ts`, `package.json`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/mcp.ts` (1 file, pure types + helpers): `McpSamplingMessage` (`role: "user" | "assistant" | "system"`, `content: { type: string; text?: string }`); `McpSamplingParams` (`messages: McpSamplingMessage[]`, `maxTokens: number`, `model?: string`, `systemPrompt?: string`, `temperature?: number`, `stopSequences?: string[]`); `McpSamplingResult` (`role: "assistant"`, `content: { type: string; text: string }`, `model?: string`); `McpSamplingLogEntry` (`server: string`, `model?: string`, `maxTokens: number`, `messageCount: number`, `allowed: boolean`, `ok: boolean`, `error?: string`, `at: number`); `mcpSamplingParamsToMessages(params) → { role, content: string }[]` (pure: maps roles, takes `content.text`, prepends `systemPrompt` as a leading system message when present; empty/invalid input → `[]`); `mcpSamplingResultToText(result) → string` (extract `content.text`, `""` when absent). No `vscode` import.
  - **S-002** — `src/mcp.ts` (1 file): `McpJsonRpc` — new `public onRequest?: (method: string, params: unknown, respond: (r: { result?: unknown; error?: { code: number; message: string } }) => void) => void`; in `handleLine`, when a message has a numeric `id` NOT in `pending` AND a string `method` AND `onRequest` is set → invoke it with a `respond` closure that writes `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result | error }` to the output stream (guard `closed`); otherwise keep current behavior. `McpClient` — new `setSamplingHandler(cb: ((server: string, params: McpSamplingParams) => Promise<McpSamplingResult>) | undefined)` that sets `rpc.onRequest` to a closure: only handles `sampling/createMessage`, awaits `cb` (catch → JSON-RPC error code `-32000` with the error message), responds with `{ result }` on success; any other server-initiated method is answered with error `-32601 method not found` (never left unanswered — an unanswered request can hang the server). `McpHttpClient` — same `setSamplingHandler`; in `post()`, after parsing the response body, detect a server-initiated request (message with numeric `id` !== the client's own `msg.id` AND a string `method`) and answer it by POSTing `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result | error }` back (session header echoed); the client's own response is still resolved as today.
  - **S-003** — `src/mcpManager.ts` (1 file): `McpClientLike` += `setSamplingHandler(cb | undefined)`; `McpManager` — `private samplingAllowed = new Map<string, boolean>()`, `private samplingLog: McpSamplingLogEntry[] = []`, `private samplingCb: ((server: string, params: McpSamplingParams) => Promise<McpSamplingResult>) | undefined`; `setSamplingAllowed(name, allowed)` (absent/`undefined` = allow); `isSamplingAllowed(name) → boolean` (default `true`); `setSamplingHandler(cb)` — stores `cb` and (re)wires the handler on every currently running client; `ensureStarted` wires the handler on newly started clients; the per-client handler closure: `!isSamplingAllowed(server)` → log entry `{ allowed: false, ok: false }` + JSON-RPC error `sampling denied for server '<name>'`; else call `cb` (absent cb → error `sampling not configured`), success → log `{ allowed: true, ok: true }` + result, failure → log `{ ok: false, error }` + JSON-RPC error; log capped at 100 (drop oldest); `getSamplingLog() → McpSamplingLogEntry[]` (copy). `dispose()` clears the map/log.
  - **S-004** — `src/config.ts` + `src/presets.ts` (2 files): `LlmSettings` += `mcpSamplingConfirm: boolean` (default `true`) + `mcpSamplingAllowed: Record<string, boolean>` (default `{}`); `readSettings` reads `llm.mcp.sampling.confirm` and `llm.mcp.sampling.allowed` (coerce non-object → `{}`).
  - **S-005** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): in the constructor (where `mcpManager` is available), call `mcpManager.setSamplingHandler(async (server, params) => { ... })`: (1) `mcpManager.setSamplingAllowed` is synced from `settings.mcpSamplingAllowed` each turn (in `handleSend`, next to the existing `setServers` call); (2) confirmation: when `settings.mcpSamplingConfirm` and `!confirmedSamplingServers.has(server)` → `postMessage({ type: "sampling_request", server, model: params.model ?? "", maxTokens: params.maxTokens, messageCount: params.messages.length })` and await a new `pendingSamplingApproval` resolver (same pattern as `waitForApproval`; webview `sampling_approval` message → `{ approved: boolean }`); deny → throw `Error("sampling denied by user")`; approve → add server to the in-memory `Set`; (3) build the request: `messages = mcpSamplingParamsToMessages(params)`, `model = params.model || settings.model || toolbar model`, `max_completion_tokens = params.maxTokens`, `temperature`/`stop` from params when present; (4) `for await (const chunk of this.client.chatStream(body))` accumulate `chunk.content` (no tools, no streaming UI); (5) write one line to the extension output channel (`[mcp-sampling] <server> model=<model> maxTokens=<n> ok`); (6) return `{ role: "assistant", content: { type: "text", text } }`. New webview message case `sampling_approval` resolves `pendingSamplingApproval`. Never let a sampling failure crash the chat turn — all errors become JSON-RPC errors via the manager.
  - **S-006** — `src/chat/webview.ts` (1 file): handle `sampling_request` host message → render a compact confirmation card in the chat flow (title `MCP sampling request`, body: server name, model, max tokens, message count; two buttons `Approve` / `Deny`); button click → `postMessage({ type: "sampling_approval", approved: true|false })` and mark the card resolved (approved → `$(check) approved`, denied → `$(x) denied`). Reuse existing card/button styling; no new host state beyond the card.
  - **S-007** — `package.json` (1 file): contribute `llm.mcp.sampling.confirm` (boolean, default `true`, description "Ask for confirmation before an MCP server may sample the model") and `llm.mcp.sampling.allowed` (object, default `{}`, description "Per-server sampling allow/deny map; absent or true = allow").
  - **S-008** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new assertions — `mcpSamplingParamsToMessages` (role mapping, systemPrompt prepended, empty input → `[]`); `mcpSamplingResultToText` (text, missing → `""`); `McpJsonRpc.onRequest` (fake server sends `sampling/createMessage` with an id → handler invoked, response written back with matching id + result; error path writes `error`); `McpClient.setSamplingHandler` end-to-end over PassThrough streams (client responds to a server sampling request with the callback's result; callback throw → JSON-RPC error; unknown method → `-32601`); `McpManager` sampling policy (denied server → error + log entry `allowed: false`; allowed + stub cb → result + log entry `ok: true`; cb throw → error + log `ok: false`; log capped at 100; `setSamplingHandler` wired on clients started after registration); static source checks: `ChatViewProvider` registers `setSamplingHandler` + handles `sampling_approval` + posts `sampling_request`; `webview.ts` renders the sampling card; `config.ts` reads both settings; `package.json` contributes both. Gate **843 → 858** (+15).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** compile passes; smoke 858/858; a stdio MCP server that sends `sampling/createMessage` receives a valid JSON-RPC response (assistant text) after the user approves the first-use confirmation; denial (user or per-server setting) returns a JSON-RPC error and the server never hangs; every sampling request appears in the in-memory log (`getSamplingLog`) and the output channel; servers that never sample are unaffected (no behavior change); no new deps.
- **Risks:** HTTP transport: server requests can arrive inside the SSE body of ANY client request (not just `tools/call`) — the detection (numeric id ≠ own id + method) must run on every parsed response body; a server that sends a sampling request and never reads the response can still block (out of scope — documented); `maxTokens` from the server is used verbatim as `max_completion_tokens` (no cap — local model, acceptable); the confirmation `Set` is session-only (re-asks after reload — matches "confirmation on first use"); concurrent sampling requests from the same server while a confirmation is pending: the second request awaits the same pending approval (single `pendingSamplingApproval` slot, same as tool approvals — documented limitation); `McpHttpClient` answering a server request with a POST while another client request is in flight is fine (each POST is independent, session header shared).
